cardTutorial1.title: Tutorial: Introduction
cardTutorial1.welcome: Hello there! Thank you for using GM Screen!
cardTutorial1.diy: This app is not a ready-made screen, but rather a simple way for you to create your own.
cardTutorial1.use: You can use it directly in your browser on any device, or save a version as PDF if you prefer.
cardTutorial1.menus: On the left sidebar (or at the bottom on smaller screens), there are four menus:
cardTutorial1.cards: This is where the cards live. Just choose one and click where you want it to appear. The menu stays open so you can select more. You can also use the search bar to find something specific.
cardTutorial1.theme: Here you can select one of the predefined themes to change the look.
cardTutorial1.lang: Where you can change the language.

cardTutorial2.title: Tutorial: Anatomy
cardTutorial2.names: The Board is your screen. It has several Decks, where you place the Cards.
cardTutorial2.space: Cards are automatically spaced out, but if you prefer, you can adjust this using the Spacing Card.
cardTutorial2.buttons: Besides the content, cards can have 4 buttons:
cardTutorial2.tooltip: Displays more information about that card.
cardTutorial2.edit: To enter edit mode, allowing you to change details of the card.
cardTutorial2.move: You can reposition the card by clicking this button and then selecting where you want it to go.
cardTutorial2.close: Removes that card from the board.
cardTutorial2.newDeck: This button appears at the end of the board and is used to add more Decks.

cardTutorial3.title: Tutorial: Saving
cardTutorial3.login: This app has no login and does not collect any of your data. You need to save your information manually.
cardTutorial3.localStorage: The simplest way is by using the browser’s local storage (not automatic).
cardTutorial3.export: You can also export your board in .json format, allowing you to share it across devices.
cardTutorial3.pdf: Using your browser’s print menu, you can save as PDF. Adjust the paper settings to your preference.
